title: Supreme Court Upholds War Injury Pension for Soldier's Rheumatoid Arthritis During Operation Rakshak
case_name: Union of India v. Narender Kumar
card_summary: The Supreme Court upheld a war injury pension for a veteran who developed rheumatoid arthritis while posted under Operation Rakshak in Kargil, dismissing the Centre's appeal. The government argued the policy covers only specially notified operations, not an ongoing deployment like Rakshak. The Court found no such distinction in the policy text and told the Ministry to clarify this each time it notifies an operation.
card_tip: Where a pension policy notifies an operation without carving out an exception, test any government argument for narrowing coverage against the policy's actual text, not administrative convenience.
verification_notes: Confirmed by multiple independent reports (Verdictum, LiveLaw, LawChakra, Courtbook) agreeing on parties, citation, bench (Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe) and holding; judgment itself not accessed.
